quests.instruction: After weeks of searching, you get the call: your offer was accepted.
options: Narrow pitch, low start — neutral report
quests.hint: The news is very welcome. Listen to how much pitch movement the speaker uses on 'got'.
quests.explanation: Happiness widens the pitch range and raises the starting point. A neutral report would keep the pitch narrow and low.
quests.pitchRule: 😊 Happiness shows up as a wider, higher pitch range.

quests.instruction: You are telling a coworker where you left the report.
quests.word: The report is on your desk.
quests.textToSpeak: The report is on your desk.
quests.hint: This is plain information with no emotion. Notice how little the pitch moves.
quests.explanation: With no emotional content, the pitch stays compact and steady. A wide, bouncing fall would sound oddly excited.
quests.pitchRule: 😐 A neutral message keeps the pitch range small and steady.

quests.instruction: After four days of storms, you look out of the window.
quests.hint: A word like 'finally' carries feeling. Where does the speaker's voice lift?
quests.explanation: 'Finally' lifts the pitch and gives the fall a warm, satisfied shape. A flat delivery would remove the relief from the sentence.
quests.pitchRule: 😊 A lifted 'finally' adds warmth to an otherwise plain statement.

quests.instruction: A colleague pitches an idea you genuinely like.
quests.hint: The compliment is only believable if the voice matches. Listen for the peak.
quests.explanation: Genuine interest shows in a wide peak on the key word. If the same words were flat, listeners would hear polite disinterest.
quests.pitchRule: 🎯 Genuine interest is heard in a peak on the key word.

quests.instruction: Your friend mentions starting a pottery class, and you're curious.
options: Rising energy, mild lift at the end — invites more
Low, flat fall at the end — closes the topic politely
quests.correctAnswer: Rising energy, mild lift at the end — invites more
quests.hint: You want your friend to keep talking. Which ending welcomes more information?
quests.explanation: A lifted ending keeps the door open. A flat fall would sound like a polite way to change the subject.
quests.pitchRule: 📈 A lifted ending on an invitation shows real curiosity.

quests.instruction: Your neighbor shows you the third set of holiday photos, and you are tired.
options: Flat, low fall — polite, not engaged
quests.correctAnswer: Flat, low fall — polite, not engaged
quests.hint: The words are positive, but the situation suggests fatigue. Which delivery fits?
quests.explanation: A low, narrow fall on 'nice' is the standard way to be polite without engaging. It sounds friendly but closes the topic.
quests.pitchRule: 😐 Polite disinterest is low, flat and quick.

quests.instruction: Your teammate proposes a plan, and you have real doubts.
quests.word: I'm not sure that will work.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm not sure that will work.
quests.hint: You have doubts, but you haven't decided. Listen to how 'work' ends.
quests.explanation: A fall-rise on the last word signals that the matter is not settled. A firm fall would close it as a rejection.
quests.pitchRule: ↘️↗️ A fall-rise keeps doubt on the table.

quests.instruction: You've tested the solution three times and it's stable.
quests.hint: You have evidence. Ask which delivery matches that certainty.
quests.explanation: A high peak on 'definitely' and a clean fall tell the listener that you have no doubts. A fall-rise would undercut the claim.
quests.pitchRule: 📉 Certainty starts high on the key word and falls cleanly.

quests.instruction: Your colleague argues a point and you are half-convinced.
quests.hint: 'Might' already shows hesitation. Listen to whether the sentence really closes.
quests.explanation: A fall-rise on 'right' shows you are not fully convinced. A clean fall would suggest you agreed.
quests.pitchRule: ↘️↗️ A fall-rise on the last word says 'yes, but'.

quests.instruction: Your brother keeps asking the same question and you've already answered.
quests.hint: You've lost patience. Listen to how quickly and sharply the pitch drops.
quests.explanation: Annoyance produces a sharp, narrow drop, and the words seem clipped. A patient reminder would fall gently.
quests.pitchRule: 😠 Annoyance uses a sharp, tight fall.

quests.instruction: Your friend arrived an hour late, and you're hurt but hiding it.
quests.hint: The words say one thing and the voice may say another. Which delivery fits the situation?
quests.explanation: A flat, clipped fall on 'really' reveals that the speaker isn't fine. A warm, wide fall would make the reassurance believable.
quests.pitchRule: 😠 Flat delivery can undo polite words.

quests.instruction: A colleague who was due an hour ago finally walks in, and you have been waiting.
quests.word: Do you have any idea how long I've been waiting?
quests.textToSpeak: Do you have any idea how long I've been waiting?
options: Rise on 'waiting' — a real question about time
quests.hint: Ask yourself whether the speaker wants a number of minutes as an answer.
quests.explanation: Although the sentence has yes/no form, it is a complaint. A sharp fall on 'waiting' shows that no answer is expected, while a rise would invite the colleague to say how long.
quests.pitchRule: 😠 A yes/no question can fall when it is really a complaint.

quests.instruction: Your friend was missing for hours and has just walked in.
quests.hint: The danger has passed. Listen to the pace and the shape of the fall.
quests.explanation: Relief slows down the voice and lets the fall stretch out, as if the speaker were exhaling. Worry is faster and more tense.
quests.pitchRule: 😮‍💨 Relief is slower, with a long fall.

quests.instruction: Your parcel with an important gift finally arrived.
quests.word: It arrived on time after all.
quests.textToSpeak: It arrived on time after all.
quests.hint: 'After all' hints at earlier worry. Which delivery matches?
quests.explanation: A slower, sighing fall on 'all' communicates that the speaker had been anxious. Quick and flat would sound like an ordinary update.
quests.pitchRule: 😮‍💨 A sighing fall shows that a worry has ended.

quests.instruction: Your friend has just done something reckless and costly, and you are furious.
quests.word: What on earth were you thinking?
quests.textToSpeak: What on earth were you thinking?
options: Sharp fall on 'thinking' — exasperation, not a real question
Rise on 'thinking' — genuine curiosity about the reason
quests.correctAnswer: Sharp fall on 'thinking' — exasperation, not a real question
quests.hint: The speaker is upset. Would they actually wait to hear a reason?
quests.explanation: The WH-question is a rebuke, so it drops sharply on 'thinking'. A rise would sound as though the speaker really wanted an explanation.
quests.pitchRule: 😠 A sharp fall turns a 'why' question into a rebuke.

quests.instruction: Your friend just stumbled badly on the stairs.
options: Bright, quick rise on 'okay' — casual check-in
Soft, lowered rise on 'okay' — genuine concern
quests.correctAnswer: Soft, lowered rise on 'okay' — genuine concern
quests.hint: The speaker actually cares about the answer. Listen to how gentle the rise is.
quests.explanation: Concern lowers the voice and softens the rise. A bright, quick rise would sound like a routine question.
quests.pitchRule: 💛 Concern is softer and lower than a casual check.

quests.instruction: A colleague seems pale and quiet.
quests.hint: The sentence is an observation, but with care. Which delivery shows care?
quests.explanation: A gentle, lowered fall makes the observation a caring one. A flat delivery would sound like a clinical remark.
quests.pitchRule: 💛 A low, gentle fall adds care to an observation.

quests.instruction: You share an honest worry with your manager.
quests.word: I'm a bit worried about the deadline.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm a bit worried about the deadline.
options: Slow, lowered fall on 'deadline' — real worry
quests.correctAnswer: Slow, lowered fall on 'deadline' — real worry
quests.hint: 'A bit' softens the words. Which voice tells the truth?
quests.explanation: A slower fall shows that the worry is real, even though 'a bit' plays it down. A light and quick delivery would suggest it was minor.
quests.pitchRule: 💛 A slower pace shows that the worry is serious.

quests.instruction: You're inviting a friend to your birthday party and want them there.
options: Even, low delivery on 'absolutely' — polite formality
High start on 'absolutely', wide fall — enthusiastic
quests.correctAnswer: High start on 'absolutely', wide fall — enthusiastic
quests.hint: The invitation is warm and you really mean it. Listen to how the pitch starts.
quests.explanation: High energy on 'absolutely' and a wide fall shows genuine enthusiasm. An even delivery would make the invitation sound like an obligation.
quests.pitchRule: 🎉 Enthusiasm starts high and moves widely.

quests.instruction: Your friend asks about the concert you clearly didn't enjoy.
quests.hint: The words are neutral. Which delivery reveals the truth?
quests.explanation: A flat, low fall on 'fine' shows that the speaker was not impressed. A wide rise-fall would give the opposite message.
quests.pitchRule: 😐 Flat delivery can turn 'fine' into 'not great'.

quests.instruction: You have tickets for a long-awaited show tomorrow.
quests.word: I can't wait to see it!
quests.textToSpeak: I can't wait to see it!
quests.hint: The words are strong. Which voice matches?
quests.explanation: A high, wide range makes the sentence sound genuinely excited. A narrow, low delivery would suggest reluctance.
quests.pitchRule: 🎉 A wide range makes an excited sentence believable.

quests.instruction: Someone makes a claim you don't believe.
quests.hint: The words seem to agree. Listen for how the voice really responds.
quests.explanation: A flat and slightly lifted ending signals that you're not convinced. Warm agreement would fall clearly.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 A flat, slightly lifted ending signals polite doubt.

quests.instruction: You suspect someone has been lying.
quests.hint: You don't trust the source. Which word carries your suspicion?
quests.explanation: Stress on 'told' suggests that what he told you is unreliable. A neutral rise would only check what you heard.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 Stress on 'told' can suggest that the source is not trusted.

quests.instruction: A friend describes a suspiciously cheap flight.
quests.word: That seems a bit too good to be true.
quests.textToSpeak: That seems a bit too good to be true.
options: Bright fall with stress on 'good' — delighted
quests.hint: You are not celebrating. Where does the doubt land?
quests.explanation: A fall-rise with stress on 'too' signals that you suspect a catch. A bright fall would sound like admiration.
quests.pitchRule: 🤨 Stress on 'too' introduces doubt about an offer.

quests.instruction: You bump into an old friend in a foreign city.
quests.word: I didn't expect to see you here!
quests.textToSpeak: I didn't expect to see you here!
options: Low, narrow fall on 'you' — annoyed surprise
High peak on 'you', wide fall — surprised and pleased
quests.correctAnswer: High peak on 'you', wide fall — surprised and pleased
quests.hint: This is a joyful surprise. Listen for the peak.
quests.explanation: A high peak on 'you' and a wide fall convey happy astonishment. A low, narrow fall would suggest disappointment.
quests.pitchRule: 😲 Happy surprise is high, wide and lively.

quests.instruction: You walk in to find a huge dinner on the table.
quests.hint: The quantity of food is remarkable. Listen for the size of the rise.
quests.explanation: A wide rise suggests admiration and astonishment. A narrow rise would ask whether it was true in a business-like way.
quests.pitchRule: 😲 A wide rise shows admiration as well as a question.

quests.instruction: A manager announces a change nobody saw coming, and you're wary.
options: Level start, slight drop — wary surprise
quests.correctAnswer: Level start, slight drop — wary surprise
quests.hint: The word 'well' warns that not everything is positive. Listen to the level start.
quests.explanation: A cautious speaker keeps the pitch restrained after 'well'. A thrilled reaction would jump higher.
quests.pitchRule: 😲 Wary surprise stays restrained and low.

quests.instruction: After an exhausting presentation, the room finally empties.
quests.hint: The speaker is drained. Which delivery matches the situation?
quests.explanation: A long, sighing fall shows relief and exhaustion together. A bright, wide peak would suggest excitement.
quests.pitchRule: 😮‍💨 Relief has a slow, sighing fall.

quests.instruction: Your friend suggests a hike, and you're not thrilled about it.
quests.word: I suppose we could try it.
quests.textToSpeak: I suppose we could try it.
quests.hint: 'I suppose' shows hesitation. Listen to how the sentence ends.
quests.explanation: A fall-rise on 'try' keeps the decision open and shows reluctance. A firm fall would commit to the plan.
quests.pitchRule: ↘️↗️ Reluctance uses a fall-rise.

quests.instruction: A colleague announces a big contract has been won.
quests.hint: This is shared good news. Which delivery makes the compliment real?
quests.explanation: A wide rise-fall reveals sincere delight. A narrow, flat delivery would suggest politeness only.
quests.pitchRule: 🎉 Genuine delight uses a wide, energetic rise-fall.
